PullRequest.Title: mediaPreview: warn when a media file's audio codec can't be played
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #343048

The video and audio previews now warn when a file's audio uses a codec that can't be played, and suggest opening the file in an external application, so users don't think the file is broken. For example:

> This video's audio uses the AAC codec, which can't be played in the video preview. Open the file in an external application to hear its audio.

For an audio file that fails to load, the warning replaces the generic "An error occurred while loading the audio file." message.

### Why the container is parsed

Chromium silently drops audio tracks it can't decode: a video whose AAC audio can't be decoded plays with no error, no tracks and no decoded audio, just like a video without audio. Since #343490, `canPlayType` and `MediaSource.isTypeSupported` report codec support correctly, but they need the codec as input, and nothing in the browser or Electron exposes the codecs of a file. So the new `readMediaInfo` (`mediaPreview/common/mediaCodecs.ts`) reads the container and the codecs of the tracks of MP4, WebM, Ogg and WAV files, and the webview checks them against the runtime.

### Notes for reviewers

- **Reads are bounded.** Files are read in cached 64 KiB chunks through `readFileStream`, up to 2 MiB. `readFile` reads whole files whenever the provider can, even with `position` and `length`. Providers that can only read whole files, such as the Agent Host file system used for remote agent sessions, are read once and only up to 64 MiB. Reads never extend past the end of the file, which avoids a truncation bug in `readFileIntoStream` that's fixed separately in #346572; this PR doesn't depend on it.
- **The webview requests the codecs** when its content loads, and the input answers from a read started when rendering. Messages posted to the webview are lost when it's recreated, such as when the editor moves to another window.
- **The WebM fallback** that plays WebM files through Media Source Extensions in builds whose FFmpeg lacks WebM (#195758) now gets the codecs of all tracks from the same parser, instead of searching the first 64 KiB of the file for codec IDs. It asks for them before reading the file, so other formats are no longer read completely. For files that can only be read as a whole, it reads up to 200 MiB, which is the fallback's own limit.
- Only audio codecs produce a warning; the warning is text only.
- WAV formats that browsers play although `canPlayType` only recognizes PCM (IEEE float, A-law, mu-law, MP3) are never reported.

### How to test

1. In a product build, open a video with AAC audio (for example `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc=duration=3 -f lavfi -i sine=duration=3 -c:v libx264 -c:a aac narrated.mp4`). The video plays and the warning above it names AAC.
2. In Code OSS, which can play AAC, use AC-3 audio instead (`-c:a ac3`) to see the warning, and an IMA ADPCM WAV file (`-c:a adpcm_ima_wav`) to see the warning replace the audio preview's load error.
3. Videos with supported audio, such as VP9 and Opus in WebM, show no warning.

Validation:

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/mediaPreview/test/common/mediaCodecs.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/mediaPreview/test/browser/mediaPreviewEditorInputs.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/mediaPreview/test/common/mediaPreview.test.ts`: passed (11 tests).
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `pnpm run eslint` on the changed files: passed.
- The parser identified the audio codecs of 21 files encoded with ffmpeg (AAC, Opus, MP3, FLAC, AC-3, E-AC-3 and ALAC in MP4, Opus and Vorbis in WebM, Vorbis, Opus and FLAC in Ogg, and PCM, float and ADPCM WAV files). It read 247 KB of a 21.6 MB MP4 whose track descriptions are at the end.
- In Code OSS, the warning showed for AC-3 video and ADPCM audio, not for Opus WebM, and still showed after moving the editor to a new window. Insiders reports AAC and Opus in MP4 as unsupported to both `canPlayType` and `MediaSource.isTypeSupported`.
- The WebM fallback played a VP9 WebM file with the Insiders FFmpeg library, which can't open WebM.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The capability branch, full-buffer implementation, 64/200 MiB bounds, and sequential WebM call flow are all explicit in repository code. Only prevalence of large media on non-range providers is uncertain, which is reflected in medium severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: whole-media-file bytes transferred over provider RPC/IPC plus the corresponding in-memory buffers
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added cost is O(file size) per render for files up to 64 MiB, and up to 200 MiB on the WebM fallback; repeated file-change renders repeat that transfer because each readMediaInfo call creates a new reader.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: large duplicate IPC/network transfers, playback startup delay on the WebM fallback, and transient memory/GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Media previews did not read the file through IFileService to discover codecs. In particular, the WebM fallback fetched the media once in the webview and derived its codec type from those same bytes before appending them to MediaSource.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: When a provider lacks FileReadStream/FileOpenReadWriteClose, createReader now calls readFile and buffers the entire media file merely to parse metadata. The normal render allows 64 MiB, while _postWebmType retries with a 200 MiB allowance and only then lets the webview fetch the same file for MediaSource playback.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line `content ??= fileService.readFile(resource).then(file => file.value);` introduces a whole-file provider read in the codec parser; the same diff wires that parser into every render and into the WebM fallback before the existing webview fetch.
Findings.Title: Avoid whole-file codec reads on non-range providers
Findings.Impact: Opening media from providers such as the Agent Host filesystem (which exposes only FileReadWrite and base64-decodes a whole resourceRead result) or ordinary extension filesystems without the proposed chunk API transfers and buffers the entire file. For a 100–200 MiB WebM on a build that needs the existing MSE fallback, this new full-file RPC is sequentially on the playback critical path and is followed by a second full fetch, roughly doubling bytes and delaying playback; even an MP3 under 64 MiB is fully read although this parser cannot identify MP3 files.
Findings.Evidence: createReader selects this branch specifically when range/stream capabilities are absent, and line 100 invokes fileService.readFile, whose service/provider path materializes the full Uint8Array. AHPFileSystemProvider advertises FileReadWrite but neither range capability and implements readFile by resourceRead(...Base64) followed by decodeBase64. The changed _postWebmType awaits readMediaInfo(..., 200 MiB) before replying, while the changed webview waits for that reply before readMedia fetches the complete media. The deleted fallback instead called readWebm once and computed getWebmType(bytes) from that same buffer.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not use readFile for codec discovery on providers without range support. For the MSE fallback, parse the codecs from the same bytes the webview already fetches (or otherwise share that single read); for normal warnings, skip/strictly cap unsupported whole-file providers and short-circuit formats such as MP3 that the parser cannot inspect.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an audio or video preview on a local/range-capable filesystem
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The webview HTML and media fetch can begin immediately after render; codec parsing runs in parallel, so only the warning is gated on it. If direct WebM playback fails, the already-started media-info promise becomes part of the fallback critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat the media and read up to 32 positional 64 KiB streams for container metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One added stat plus 1–32 range reads per render, depending on metadata placement and parser structure limits
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No IFileService metadata scan occurred; only the webview's media resource load read the media.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Normally off the direct-playback critical path but required before the codec warning; it is on the MSE fallback path if direct playback fails.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Webview media resource fetch for playback
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One media load per render, with an additional full fetch only when the existing MSE fallback takes over
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same media load existed before the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One media file per open editor; parsing reads 64 KiB chunks for file structures encountered, capped at 32 distinct chunks (2 MiB) per render.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Chunk reads within one parser are sequential and cached by chunk index. The parser runs concurrently with the webview's existing media load, and separate editors are not globally limited.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A render coalesces its webview codec requests through one _mediaInfo promise and caches chunks within that parse. There is no cache across renders or editor instances; failures/unsupported formats resolve undefined and are reused only for that render.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the render call, parser limits, promise reuse, and stream-read loop are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual metadata placement determines whether one or many chunks are read, and local disk reads may be cheap.
Scenarios.Verdict: Bounded range reads are reasonable in isolation; no separate finding beyond the non-range whole-file mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open media from an Agent Host or extension filesystem without range/stream capabilities
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new parser starts during render in parallel with direct playback, but consumes the same provider/connection resources. Codec warning delivery waits for the full read; provider contention can also delay the media fetch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider readFile transfers and buffers the complete media resource; Agent Host resourceRead uses base64 and then decodes it
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One newly added full-file RPC per render for files at most 64 MiB, in addition to the playback resource load
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The workbench did not perform this extra whole-file codec read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Parallel to initial direct playback but gates warnings and competes for bandwidth, provider concurrency, and memory.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Webview fetches the media for direct playback
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing media load per render
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This was the only media-content read needed for normal playback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Direct playback depends on it; the added parser can overlap and contend with it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Media file byte size up to the 64 MiB normal-render threshold; unsupported MP3 files are included even though the parser returns no media info.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One whole-file parser read per editor/render runs concurrently with the webview media fetch. Agent Host limits readFile operations globally to 10, so multiple previews or updates queue and contend for that limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The entire-file promise is cached only within one ChunkedReader invocation. _mediaInfo coalesces requests for one render, but there is no cross-render cache or negative cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: capability checks force this branch, readFile materializes the complete file, and Agent Host advertises no range capability.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence and bandwidth of large files on these providers varies, but the byte count and duplicate boundary are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff adds an O(file-size) whole-file transfer/allocation for metadata, including formats it cannot parse.

Scenarios.Scenario: Play WebM through the existing Media Source Extensions fallback after direct playback fails
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The webview waits for get-webm-type. If the initial parser returned undefined, the input synchronously completes a second parser attempt with a 200 MiB whole-file allowance before replying; only then does the webview fetch bytes and append them to MediaSource.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and base64/decode the complete WebM to discover track codecs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-file RPC up to 200 MiB when the initial 64 MiB-limited attempt returned undefined
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No backend file-service read occurred on this fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly blocks the response that permits MSE fallback playback to proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the complete media in the webview and concatenate it for MediaSource
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-file fetch up to 200 MiB
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous fallback fetched once and computed the WebM type from the same bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs only after codec-type resolution and supplies the playback buffer.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One WebM file, especially 64–200 MiB on a provider without range support; track/header structure controls only range-provider reads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The backend codec read and webview full fetch are sequential on this path, not coalesced into one transfer. Within the parser reads are sequential; Agent Host's read limiter may add queueing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The initial _mediaInfo result is reused when successful. An undefined result is not negatively terminal for fallback and causes one retry with the larger threshold; no fetched media bytes are shared with the webview.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the message ordering and awaits make the two complete reads sequential, while the deleted code proves the previous single-buffer behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Only builds/files that fail normal WebM playback enter this path, and provider speed varies.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable as the most severe manifestation of the submitted whole-file-read finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keep a changing/generated media file open in the preview
Scenarios.CriticalPath: File events schedule render after 100 ms. Each render reloads the webview and starts a new codec parse; parsing is not awaited by _render and older parses are only ignored after completion, not cancelled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeat stat and range/full-file codec parsing for each scheduled render
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One added parse per coalesced 100 ms update window; 1–32 range reads or one whole-file read per parse
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Renders already reloaded the media webview, but did not also launch codec parsing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Usually background work, but overlaps later renders and can contend with the current media load.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload the media resource after each render
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing media reload per scheduled render
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This reload and the 100 ms scheduling behavior already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Needed to display the updated media.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of update windows while the file remains open, multiplied by file size for whole-file providers or by up to 32 chunks for range providers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Events within a 100 ms window coalesce, but a later window can start another parse while a slow prior parse is still running. There is no shared parse limiter; Agent Host's provider-level limiter bounds only whole-file read execution to 10.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each render replaces _mediaInfo and creates a fresh ChunkedReader/cache. Identity checks suppress stale posts but do not cancel or share reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: RunOnceScheduler does not await its runner, _render does not await readMediaInfo, and no cancellation token is passed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Update frequency and provider latency depend on the producer; continuously generated media is less common than a single open.
Scenarios.Verdict: This amplifies the submitted whole-file finding through repeated/overlapping reads; it does not require a separate duplicate comment.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files. One medium-severity regression was submitted: non-range providers now buffer entire media files for codec metadata, and the WebM fallback can add a sequential duplicate read of up to 200 MiB before the existing playback fetch. Range-capable parsing is bounded and cached per render; no concrete regression fix suitable for blame-based learning was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
